scope: Proposition 2.3 (Small repulsive coupling) of the manuscript “A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation” (preprints/A-Coulomb-Ground-State-Density-without-Kohn-Sham-Ensemble-Representation-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 278 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5a9d714fd656a2c9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix D ≥ 100. For all sufficiently small λ ≥ 0, the ionic operator H2,λ has a simple isolated ground state, and H3,λ has a simple isolated ground state Ψλ in the sector Sz = 1/2. Its energy is an absolute ground energy of H3,λ. The ionic ground state is a spin singlet, is even under simultaneous reflection of its two spatial coordinates, and is axisymmetric. The state Ψλ is real, axisymmetric, and odd under simultaneous reflection of its three spatial coordinates. The states and energies can be chosen analytic near zero; in particular, their state vectors converge with error O(λ) in H2. At zero coupling, Ψ0 = b ↑ ∧b ↓ ∧e ↑, E2(0) = 2ϵb, E3(0) = 2ϵb + ϵe. (2.9) The ionic state has spatial factor b(x1)b(x2) and the normalized singlet spin factor.
